id.description: Identifier of the item, assigned when it is created

expand.description: Relations to add to each item of the answer, by name; null adds none

query.description: Text to search for in the items; null or no value returns every item

created_on.description: When the item was created (ISO 8601, UTC)

modified_on.description: When the item was last changed (ISO 8601, UTC)

user_id.description: Identifier of the user who owns the item

certificate_id.description: Certificate ID: a server certificate (not an mTLS CA) with its files present, 0 for none, or new to request one

domain_names.description: Domain names the host answers for, one to 100, each once

items.description: A host name, a wildcard name or a regular expression starting with ~ (nginx server_name); a name that is not a regular expression has no nginx syntax characters

enabled.description: Whether the host is active; a disabled host stays saved but is left out of the nginx config

ssl_forced.description: Whether plain HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS (needs a certificate)

hsts_enabled.description: Whether the Strict-Transport-Security header is sent (needs a certificate and forced HTTPS)

hsts_subdomains.description: Whether the HSTS header also covers every subdomain (includeSubDomains)

ssl_provider.description: Where the certificate comes from: letsencrypt (an ACME server), other (uploaded) or mtls (a client CA)

npmpro_http3_support.description: Whether the host also listens for HTTP/3 (QUIC); needs a certificate

npmpro_nginx_online.description: Whether the nginx config of this host is loaded

npmpro_nginx_err.description: nginx error if the config of this host could not be loaded

npmpro_directory.description: Directory to group this host in the UI

npmpro_description.description: A one-line note on what this host is for, shown in the lists

npmpro_tags.description: Labels of this host for the lists, at most 10. A tag has 1 to 32 letters, digits, spaces, "-", "_" or "." and no space at either end; tags that differ only in case are one tag, the first is kept

npmpro_mtls_certificate_id.description: mTLS Certificate ID: an mTLS CA certificate with its file present, 0 for none

npmpro_mtls_verify_client_optional.description: Make the mTLS client verification optional

npmpro_mtls_bypass_auth_request.description: Skip the auth request if the mTLS client verification succeeded

npmpro_noindex.description: Send noindex header and block some user agents

email.description: Email address, used to sign in and for notices

directive.description: What the rule does to a matching address: allow or deny

address.description: A client address or network (IPv4 or IPv6, with an optional /prefix), a unix: socket, or all

access_items.description: Basic auth users, each username once

username.description: Name to sign in with; no colon or control character, each name once in the list

password.description: Password to sign in with, stored only as a hash; never part of an answer

access_clients.description: Access rules in order: rules without an address are dropped, an all rule can only be the last one

address.description: A client address or network (IPv4 or IPv6, with an optional /prefix), a unix: socket, or all

directive.description: What the rule does to a matching address: allow or deny

npmpro_comment.description: A note for the rule, shown with the rule (it is not written into the nginx config)

npmpro_access_list_ids.description: Identifiers of the access lists applied, each once; never part of an answer

npmpro_host_access_list_type.description: Which access lists protect the host: public (none) or custom (the chosen ones)

npmpro_location_access_list_type.description: Which access lists protect the location: global (the host's), public (none) or custom (the chosen ones)

certificate_key.description: Required for custom certificates, not used for mTLS certificates

npmpro_maintenance.description: Maintenance mode: every request gets the maintenance page (503), except ACME challenges

npmpro_page_not_found.description: Page for 404: global (Settings, Landing pages), npmpro (the built-in page), custom, upstream (the upstream's own answer)

npmpro_page_upstream.description: Page for 502, 503 and 504: global, npmpro, custom, upstream (the upstream's own error)

npmpro_page.description: Page of a 404 host: global, npmpro, custom

npmpro_denied_page.description: Page for 401 and 403 of an access list: global, npmpro, custom, plain (nginx's plain page)

npmpro_page_html.description: Custom page: one HTML file, at most 1 MiB in UTF-8; SSI only echo of remote_addr, date_gmt, date_local, status, host and config timefmt

npmpro_dns_records.description: The host record option: one entry per host name that gets its own DNS record (an A record, and an AAAA with `ipv6`) at the provider of the one DNS credential that covers it, kept current by the Dynamic DNS updater. Names left out are released: a record NPMpro created is deleted at the provider, an adopted one is only released. Leave the field out to keep the option as it is; an empty array turns it off. Ticking a name needs Certificates manage and a visible covering credential; without it that name answers `unavailable` and the host still saves. The answer lists the states in `npmpro_dns_records`.

name.description: A plain host name of the host

proxied.description: Cloudflare only: create the record proxied. Used when the record is created, never changed later

ipv6.description: Also an AAAA record, when a public IPv6 address was found

reach_confirmed.description: The user checked from outside that ports 80 and 443 reach this server; needed when the reach probe did not prove it
